deities: Durga (as Maa Ramchandi, form of Chandi)

history.period: Antiquity unknown; a YouTube vlog claims 8th century CE without sourcing (UNVERIFIED - verify)
history.summary: A revered Shaktipitha of western Odisha: the shrine of Maa Ramchandi sits inside a natural rock cave on the banks of the sacred Ib River, reached via an iron staircase. A remarkable feature is that the Ib River's waters touch the sanctum, and during monsoon the shrine becomes partially submerged. Local tradition holds that Lord Rama and Lakshmana's footsteps blessed this site during their journey, and the goddess is venerated as the presiding deity (guardian) of Brajarajnagar. The temple comes alive during both Chaitra and Ashwin Navratri. Not the same as the Ramachandi Temple at Konark (Puri district). Its age is unverified - one travel vlog claims an 8th-century origin, but no reliable published history was found. Coordinates are town-level for Brajarajnagar and approximate.

name: Ramchandi Temple
town_description: Brajarajnagar (also spelled Brajrajnagar) is an industrial town in Jharsuguda district of western Odisha, on the banks of the Ib River about 30 km from Jharsuguda town. It grew around coal mining and industry, and the town's presiding deity is Maa Ramchandi, whose cave shrine on the Ib riverbank is its best-known landmark. The riverbank setting makes it a scenic spot as well as a pilgrimage site.
